Unit 2 · Week 1 · Lesson 5 · Creative

Draw the monster

Your drawing. The book's words.

Today

  1. Find the details in the book
  2. Draw the monster in pencil
  3. Label it with the exact words from the book

You need: the novel, a pencil, a blank page.

01
Step 1 · The rule for labels · 2 min

A label is a quote. Copy it exactly.

  1. Inverted commas: "..."
  2. Word for word. No changes.
  3. Short: 3 to 10 words.
  4. Add the chapter: (Ch 1)
02
Step 2 · Together: is it copied exactly? · 3 min

Check each label against Chapter 1. Thumbs up or down, then click.

1. "two big arms" (Ch 1)

✗ The book says "two long arms"

2. "a green, furry skin" (Ch 1)

✓ Exact

3. a great and terrible face (Ch 1)

✗ No inverted commas

4. "Its voice rumbled low and loud" (Ch 1)

✓ Exact

5. "warm, compost smelling breath" (Ch 1)

✗ Missing the hyphen: "compost-smelling"
03
Step 3 · Detail hunt · 8 min · in your book

Find the exact words for each part. Write 5 of them in your book.

Start in Chapter 1 at "As Conor watched, the uppermost branches..." Read to the end of the chapter.

Faceclick to check"a great and terrible face"Ch 1
Armsclick to check"two long arms"Ch 1
Legsclick to check"a second leg to set down beside the main trunk"Ch 1
Bodyclick to check"a spine and then a torso"Ch 1
Skinclick to check"a green, furry skin"Ch 1
Sizeclick to check"Already taller than Conor's window"Ch 1
Handsclick to check"its giant hands"Ch 1
Eyesclick to check"its huge eyes"Ch 1
Teethclick to check"raggedy teeth made of hard, knotted wood"Ch 1
Breathclick to check"warm, compost-smelling breath"Ch 1

Finished? Chapters 5 and 7 add more: find the "chest" and the "elbows".

04
Step 4 · Plan · 2 min

Choose your moment

A

At Conor's window, its giant hands on either side.

Chapter 1

B

Holding Conor up in the night sky, against the moon.

Chapter 1

C

Standing in the back garden, bending down to Conor.

Chapter 5

Then circle 3 details from your detail hunt that your drawing will show.

05
Step 5 · Draw · 20 min · pencil only

Build it from the words

If you don't know where to start

  1. Draw the trunk first: a tall body shape.
  2. Add branches twisting into arms, hands and a second leg.
  3. At the top, tangle branches into a face: eyes, mouth, teeth.
  4. Cover it in short pencil lines for the needle-like leaves.
  5. Make it huge: add something small next to it, like a window or a house.

Remember

  • Use your ideas, not the pictures in the book.
  • Leave space around the edge for your labels.
  • Your 3 details must be easy to see.
  • Neat lines matter less than clear details.
06
Step 6 · Label and check · 7 min

Add 3 labels. Then swap with your partner.

Label

  1. Draw an arrow from the detail into the space.
  2. Write the exact words in inverted commas.
  3. Add (Ch 1) or the right chapter.
"a green, furry skin" (Ch 1)

Copy check

Swap drawings. Check one label against the book, word by word.

  • ☐ Inverted commas
  • ☐ Every word the same
  • ☐ Same punctuation
  • ☐ Chapter number

Found a mistake? Tell your partner. They fix it.

07
Step 7 · Gallery walk · 5 min

Leave your drawing on your desk. Walk round.

  1. Look at as many drawings as you can.
  2. Find one drawing where the labels match the picture perfectly.
  3. Tell its owner which label works best, and why.
I like how you showed "..." because ...
08
Step 8 · Before you go · 2 min

Which detail makes the monster feel real?

Add it to the Supernatural vs. Reality page of your Theme tracker.

ChapterClueWhat it shows
1"warm, compost-smelling breath"This shows that Conor can smell the monster, which makes it feel real.

Use the example, or choose your own detail.

Collect the drawings if you want to put them on the wall.
